title: Skip the $10k course - build an agent instead
oneliner: Don't pay $5,000-$10,000 for an executive AI course; spend a few dollars on tools and build your own AI agent, then put it in your portfolio.
says: He pushes back on the ads for big-institute AI and executive courses charging $5,000 to $10,000. His recommendation: do not spend that money and time. Instead, subscribe to the AI tools already on the market, build your own AI agent with them, and embed that work into your profile.
explained: This is his learning philosophy in its sharpest form, and it repeats across the channel: implemented proof beats purchased credentials. A course certificate tells an interviewer you attended; a working agent you built tells them you can do the job - and gives you real stories about what broke and how you fixed it, which is what interviews actually probe.

The cost asymmetry is real: serious AI tooling subscriptions run tens of dollars a month, so a few hundred dollars of building buys more signal than a five-figure program. The caveat to hold alongside: courses are not worthless for everyone - structure helps some learners. His point is about the expensive executive-track programs sold on credential prestige, not about learning itself.
takeaway: Buy tools, not certificates: one self-built agent in your portfolio outweighs a $10k course badge.
